dish: Den Special okonomiyaki (squid & pork topped with shrimp, konjac, scallops and a fried egg)
w: Cabbage-heavy, crisp-outside fluffy-inside neighbourhood okonomiyaki near Hanazonochō station; picked in OSAKA-INFO's konamon guide and Osaka Metro's Osaka Mania okonomiyaki feature, which singles out the Den Special.

dish: Anago (conger eel) sushi — steamed-eel nigiri, eel box sushi and thin rolls with a house sweet tare
w: Take-out-only conger-eel sushi shop by Sakai's Dejima fishing port, trading 70+ years on Sakai's anago tradition; picked in OSAKA-INFO's 'Sakai Gourmet Recommended by Locals' and listed by Rurubu.
Steak house founded 1988 specialising in Miyazaki black wagyu, with its own butcher shop in Sakai; listed by the Sakai Tourist & Convention Bureau and OSAKA-INFO's locals' Sakai gourmet picks.

dish: Sardine courses — 40+ preparations of Mie-landed iwashi incl. sashimi, meunière and almond-fried
w: Sardine-only Japanese restaurant buying direct from Mie fishermen; featured by the Sakai Tourist & Convention Bureau and in OSAKA-INFO's 'Sakai Gourmet Recommended by Locals'.

dish: Kashimin-yaki (thin teppan crepe of cabbage, minced kashiwa hen and beef fat) — Kishiwada's soul food
w: Seven-seat chicken shop credited with sparking the kashimin boom — most Kishiwada kashimin shops buy their chicken here; featured by Kansai Walker and JAL's OnTrip travel magazine.

dish: Wakayama chūka soba — soy-forward shoyu-tonkotsu 'shako-mae' style bowl
n: Honke Arochi Marutaka (本家アロチ 丸髙 中華そば, Wakayama)
w: Founded 1940 in Wakayama's Arochi nightlife district, the legend of the soy-led 'shako-mae' lineage and often called a root of Wakayama ramen; covered by ja.wikipedia's Wakayama ramen article, Ramen Walker and the Wakayama prefectural tourism ramen feature.
